introHeading: The mirror booth, built for Manhattan's logistics
introParas: Manhattan events run on somebody else's clock — a loading dock window, a freight elevator reservation, a building engineer who signs off at six sharp. Our magic mirror booth is built to work inside that reality: the gold frame breaks down to load-dock-friendly cases, we send your venue's certificate of insurance ahead of time, and behind the glass sits the same Canon DSLR and studio ring light that makes every print look shot in a studio rather than snapped on a phone.

It is still the booth we place most often in Midtown and Financial District hotel ballrooms, SoHo gallery spaces and Tribeca lofts, because it works across every guest list in the room — a full-length mirror lets a whole wedding party pile in at once, and grandparents use the touchscreen as happily as the after-party crowd. Ask for a fingertip signature on the print and it becomes the guest book too, which is why it is our most-requested booth for Manhattan weddings, corporate holiday parties and milestone birthdays alike.

The mirror wants a 10ft x 10ft footprint, though we compress to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance for a tighter Chelsea gallery or Hell's Kitchen private room, and it runs off one standard 110V outlet within 15 feet — ideally not shared with the DJ or catering. Setup takes about 20 minutes and we arrive a full hour before your start time so it is tested and silent before your first guest walks in. Manhattan is a standard service area, so any travel fee is quoted from your venue ZIP up front — nothing shows up on the invoice afterward.

faqHeading: Mirror Photo Booth in Manhattan — FAQ

faqs.q: Can the mirror booth get through a Manhattan building's loading dock and freight elevator?
faqs.a: Yes — we build the load-in plan around your building's loading dock window and freight elevator reservation before we arrive, which is standard for the Midtown and Financial District venues we work in most.

faqs.q: Do you provide a certificate of insurance for Manhattan hotel ballrooms and event spaces?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $2 million insurance policy and can turn around a certificate of insurance the same day you ask, addressed to your Manhattan venue's requirements.

faqs.q: How much space does the mirror booth need in a tight SoHo or Tribeca gallery?
faqs.a: Optimal is 10ft x 10ft, but we compress to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance for a smaller gallery or private dining room, and we only need one standard 110V outlet within 15 feet.

faqs.q: Is there a travel fee to bring the mirror booth into Manhattan?
faqs.a: Manhattan is a standard service area — any travel fee is quoted up front from your venue ZIP code before you book, never added to the invoice afterward.

faqs.q: Can guests sign their photo at the mirror booth?
faqs.a: Yes. The touchscreen lets guests add a signature or drawing to their print with a fingertip, which turns the photo into a keepsake rather than just a snapshot — popular at Manhattan hotel weddings where it doubles as the guest book.

faqs.q: Is an attendant included with the rental?
faqs.a: Yes. A trained attendant runs the mirror booth for your full Manhattan booking — setup, helping guests through the touchscreen, keeping the prop table tidy, and breakdown at the end of the night.

faqs.q: How long does setup take, and can you arrive early for a Financial District after-work event?
faqs.a: About 20 minutes once we are in the room. We arrive a full hour before your start time as standard; if your venue's vendor window opens earlier than that, idle time is $55 per hour.

faqs.q: Is the mirror booth a good fit for a Midtown hotel wedding?
faqs.a: It is one of our most-requested booths for Manhattan hotel weddings — the full-length format lets a whole wedding party pile in for one photo, and grandparents use the touchscreen as easily as the after-party crowd.
